profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a national law firm between the partner leading a commissioned white paper for a coalition of regional governments and the senior knowledge-management counsel supporting cross-jurisdiction drafting. The paper examines the territorial impact of COVID-19 across health, economic, social, and fiscal dimensions, with examples of how national, regional, and local governments managed the crisis and lessons for resilient multi-level governance. The immediate context is that multiple lawyers and researchers have contributed sections and jurisdiction notes, and a steering committee of public-sector clients expects a near-final package before next week's call. The agenda is to align the substantive drafting stream and the document-production stream on what Friday's 'clean draft for circulation' includes, which source set citations should map to, how the government-response matrix is being used, and how the annex will be finalized after the main text lands. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, shared artifacts, and timing so each side can proceed without another coordination call.

members.name: Elena Vargas
members.role: Partner, Public Law and Intergovernmental Affairs
members.expertise: Administrative law, emergency powers, decentralization, and policy-facing legal analysis for public-sector clients
members.background: Elena leads cross-jurisdictional advisory matters and regularly supervises fast-turnaround reports for ministries, regional associations, and multilateral bodies; she is accustomed to refining narrative framing late in the process while support teams regularize citations and appendices behind the scenes.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve flexibility to reshape examples and framing over the weekend in light of client sensitivities while still signaling that the project is under control; she also wants the steering committee to see a polished main story even if some back-end support materials are still being regularized.
hidden_assumptions: A 'clean draft' means the main text reads smoothly, has no visible tracked changes or drafting notes, and is presentable to clients even if citation checking is still underway.

The response matrix is primarily a knowledge-management work product that supports the paper but is not something the substantive team needs to actively re-validate line by line unless a legal issue is flagged.
The 'current source pack' naturally means the most up-to-date working compilation of government measures available to the team, including late materials shared informally on Thursday night.
If people say the annex can be cleaned after the draft settles, KM will handle the practical clean-up from the existing materials once the narrative team stops moving examples around.

members.name: Marcus Chen
members.expertise: Legal research workflows, citation integrity, multi-author document control, and publication-ready comparative law products
members.background: Marcus supports public-law matters by maintaining source repositories, harmonizing jurisdictional contributions, and preparing committee-ready comparative reports; he is known for converting messy multi-author drafts into stable documents where every factual claim maps to a verified source record.
members.private_state: He wants to freeze the support materials by Friday so his team can complete one controlled citation and annex pass instead of chasing weekend revisions; he is also concerned that if the matrix is treated casually, the firm will circulate a document whose examples cannot be traced cleanly across jurisdictions.
hidden_assumptions: A 'clean draft' means the version is clean not just visually but evidentially: citations checked, authorities mapped, and references stable enough that no further source-level reconciliation should be needed before circulation.

The response matrix is the master comparative record for the paper, so the substantive team is expected to confirm that its entries accurately reflect the examples and characterizations used in the draft.
The 'current source pack' means the latest frozen set uploaded to the citation tracker and validated for use, not newer materials still sitting in email chains or analyst notes.

If the annex is to be cleaned after the main draft settles, the substantive team will first confirm which jurisdiction examples and labels remain in scope, and KM will then do technical harmonization rather than substantive selection.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Friday's deliverable should be a 'clean draft for circulation.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a client-presentable main text with no tracked changes, comments, or obvious drafting clutter, even if some citations and annex links are still being finalized internally.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a version that is clean in documentary terms as well: citations verified, source mapping stable, and annex references finalized enough that it can move into circulation without another evidentiary clean-up pass.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The word 'clean' sounds like routine document hygiene and is widely used in legal practice without unpacking whether it refers to visual presentation or fully validated support apparatus, so both hear reassuring competence rather than a hidden threshold difference.

misalignment_points.topic: Whether the response matrix is a support tool or a validation artifact
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the response matrix' as the shared comparative backbone for the paper.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 treats the matrix as an internal KM support tool that organizes research behind the scenes; as long as it generally captures the examples in play, she does not see the substantive team as needing to review or sign off on it in detail.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 treats the matrix as part of the active shared work product whose scope includes being the validated record of which measures, jurisdictions, and characterizations the substantive team is actually relying on, so he expects lawyer confirmation of its entries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same artifact name and genuinely do see it as the paper's backbone, but the subtle boundary difference is about whether 'using' the matrix includes substantive validation responsibility; that boundary feels too implicit and operationally obvious to either of them to state outright.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'current source pack' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the draft should align to the 'current source pack' before Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the live working compilation of decrees, regional orders, ministry summaries, and jurisdiction notes updated through Thursday night, including documents circulated by email but not yet normalized.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the last frozen and tracker-uploaded source bundle from Wednesday afternoon that his team has already indexed and validated.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a fast-moving comparative law project, 'current' naturally sounds singular and self-evident, and both assume the other is referring to the obvious latest body of materials without distinguishing between live working inputs and the formally controlled source set.

misalignment_points.topic: Who does what when 'the annex can be cleaned afterward'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that 'the annex can be cleaned after the main draft is settled.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes KM will take the existing matrix and draft references, standardize the annex, and backfill the remaining alignment work once the narrative text stops moving.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the substantive team will first confirm which examples, jurisdiction labels, and descriptions remain in the paper, after which KM will perform formatting, harmonization, and citation checks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The passive phrase 'can be cleaned' makes the task sound like ordinary post-draft housekeeping, so neither pauses to separate substantive confirmation from technical regularization or to assign the sequencing explicitly.
